newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power remains firm amid cold forecast.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power remains firm amid cold forecast.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. were steady to stronger Monday, supported by cold weather forecasts later this week and firm natural gas prices, industry sources said.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory climbed into the $23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared to Friday's trading range for Monday around $22.00.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed around $15.00-$16.00, which is mostly unchanged.
December TVA was talked in the $22.50-22.90 area, while January/February prices for firm power were around $23.50, traders said.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks were in the $22.00-23.00 range early, but cold weather forecasts pushed prices into the $24.00-26.00 area as trading progressed.
These prices compare with Friday's trading range for Monday delivery around $25.00.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was quoted in the $15.50-17.00 range, as compared with the $17 trading range evident on Friday.

Among Florida utilities, 12-hour block power for Tuesday was mostly steady around $28.00, but some sources speculated that prices may begin to strengthen later in the week as a cold front now in Texas moves eastward.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to dip to below-normal levels by the middle of this week, with temperatures as much as 14 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal anticipated in western Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC). Slightly more moderate temperatures are forecast for eastern SERC.
Separately, Entergy Corp's 1,173 megawatt (MW) Grand Gulf 1 nuclear unit is expected to resume production this Wednesday following scheduled maintenance and refueling.
Also, Southern Nuclear's 822 MW Farley 2 nuclear unit, which has been shut for refueling, is expected to return to service in December, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
On the natural gas side, prices along the Gulf Coast for Tuesday delivery bounced into the low-$3.70s today, up about five cents from Friday's lows and up about $1 from November 1 levels.
